czar: a male monarch or emperor (especially of Russia prior to 1917)
czar alexander i: the czar of Russia whose plans to liberalize the government of Russia were unrealized because of the wars with Napoleon (1777-1825)
czar alexander ii: the son of Nicholas I who, as czar of Russia, introduced reforms that included limited emancipation of the serfs (1818-1881)
czar alexander iii: son of Alexander II who was czar of Russia (1845-1894)
czar nicholas i: czar of Russia from 1825 to 1855 who led Russia into the Crimean War (1796-1855)
czar peter i: czar of Russia who introduced ideas from western Europe to reform the government
czarina: the wife or widow of a czar
czarist: of or relating to or characteristic of a czar
czaristic: of or relating to or characteristic of a czar
czaritza: the wife or widow of a czar
czech: a native of inhabitant of the Czech Republic
of or relating to Czechoslovakia or its people or their language
czech capital: the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic in the western part of the country
czech republic: a landlocked republic in central Europe
czechoslovak: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia
czechoslovakia: a former republic in central Europe
czechoslovakian: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia
of or relating to Czechoslovakia or its people or their language
czerny: Austrian virtuoso pianist and composer of many works for the piano
czestochowa: a city of southern Poland whose church contains the statue of the black Madonna which attracts many pilgrims
